segment.description: Goforth Creek (GNIS 01328281), a Cherokee National Forest tributary of the Ocoee River in Polk County — the TWRA-stocked trout creek along the old US-64/Ocoee River gorge corridor that the catalog describes ('steep, scenic pocket water'). No USGS gauge exists on the creek (the Polk County USGS surface-water station inventory contains no GOFORTH station). TDEC's ambient monitoring station TDECWPC-GOFOR000.2PO ('U/S OF PARKING AREA AT CREEK', 35.0869, -84.5145) sits at river mile 0.2 near the mouth.
segment.boundaries: Full named creek: Ocoee River confluence at ~35.0836, -84.5147 (mouth on the Ocoee upstream of Parksville Lake) upstream to ~35.1144, -84.4796 near Boyd Gap, HUC-8 06020003 (Ocoee), per the NHD flowline query used by the wave-3 verification pass. Polk County only.

coldSource.notes: Steep forested Cherokee NF pocket-water gorge draining to the Ocoee corridor; no dam on the creek and no spring-influence documentation found. No published elevation for the creek's reach was located on an agency page. Corridor context only (NOT a statement about Goforth Creek itself): TWRA's Trout Management Plan states 'The Normandy and Ocoee tailwaters do not have cold water year-round and receive only 9-inch Rainbow Trout seasonally' — that refers to the Ocoee tailwater below the dam, not this tributary, whose own coldwater status rests on the TDEC temperature grabs recorded below.

holdover.detail: No holdover evidence found: no creel survey, stocking-location holdover note, or multiple independent angler reports were located for Goforth Creek.

wildPopulation.detail: No creek-specific wild-trout documentation found. The USFS Cherokee National Forest fishing page states generally that the forest holds 'wild trout, rainbow, brown and native brookies... above 1000 feet', but it does not name Goforth Creek, and no agency fish-community inventory for the creek was located in this or the prior verification pass.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC grabs at the creek's lower reach (0.2 mi above the Ocoee mouth) read 20.23 degC in late July 2006 and 18.71 degC in September — trout-viable summer temperatures on a steep, fully forested Cherokee NF creek — but the series is a single 2006-2008 grab set, so confidence is limited.
